Breed: Afghan Hound
        Size: large
        Description: An aristocratic sighthound of ancient lineage, prized for its silky, flowing coat and elegant, aloof demeanor.
        Origin: Afghanistan
        Breed Group: Hound
        Lifespan: 12-18 years
        Temperament: aloof, independent, clownish, dignified
        Health Considerations: Prone to hip dysplasia, hypothyroidism, and juvenile cataracts. Their deep chest makes them susceptible to bloat.
        Key Health Tips: Schedule regular eye exams and thyroid checks. Feed multiple small meals to reduce bloat risk. Brush coat several times weekly to prevent matting.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, refined, and narrow
          Ears: Long, covered in silky hair, pendant
          Coat: Long, thick, silky
          Tail: Ring-curled at the tip, feathered
        Measurements:
          Height: 25-27 inches
          Weight: 50-60 lbs

Breed: African Hunting Dog
        Size: large
        Description: A highly social and intelligent wild canid native to sub-Saharan Africa, known for its extraordinary cooperative hunting strategy.
        Origin: Sub-Saharan Africa
        Breed Group: Wild Canid
        Lifespan: 10-13 years
        Temperament: social, intelligent, energetic, cooperative
        Health Considerations: Susceptible to distemper, rabies, and other canine diseases. Inbreeding in small wild populations raises genetic health concerns.
        Key Health Tips: Not a domestic breed. Conservation efforts focus on vaccination programs and habitat preservation. Not suitable as pets.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Broad, strong, medium-length
          Ears: Large, rounded, erect
          Coat: Short, sparse, mottled
          Tail: Medium, often white-tipped
        Measurements:
          Height: 24-30 inches
          Weight: 40-70 lbs

Breed: Airedale
        Size: large
        Description: Known as the 'King of Terriers,' the Airedale is the largest terrier breed, combining athleticism with intelligence and a bold personality.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 11-14 years
        Temperament: intelligent, outgoing, confident, friendly
        Health Considerations: Can be prone to hip dysplasia, skin conditions, and hypothyroidism. Eye conditions may also occur.
        Key Health Tips: Keep coat hand-stripped or professionally groomed. Regular exercise prevents obesity. Annual thyroid and hip evaluations are recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, flat, and strong
          Ears: V-shaped, folded forward
          Coat: Dense, wiry, with soft undercoat
          Tail: Erect, carried upright, customarily docked
        Measurements:
          Height: 22-24 inches
          Weight: 50-70 lbs

Breed: American Staffordshire Terrier
        Size: medium
        Description: A muscular, stocky terrier known for its courage, strength, and deep loyalty to its family, often misunderstood due to its powerful build.
        Origin: United States
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 12-16 years
        Temperament: loyal, tenacious, courageous, friendly
        Health Considerations: Susceptible to hip dysplasia, heart disease, skin allergies, and elbow dysplasia. Cerebellar ataxia can occur in some lines.
        Key Health Tips: Maintain healthy weight to reduce joint stress. Regular vet cardiac evaluations are advised. Allergy management through diet and dermatology checks.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Medium-length, rounded on upper side
          Ears: Short, high-set, rose or half-pricked
          Coat: Short, stiff, glossy
          Tail: Short, low-set, tapering to a point
        Measurements:
          Height: 17-19 inches
          Weight: 40-70 lbs

Breed: Appenzeller
        Size: medium
        Description: A lively, versatile Swiss mountain dog historically used as a herding and draft dog, known for its tricolor coat and energetic spirit.
        Origin: Switzerland
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: lively, self-assured, reliable, fearless
        Health Considerations: Generally healthy but may experience hip dysplasia. Eye problems and hereditary conditions in the breed line should be monitored.
        Key Health Tips: Provide ample daily exercise to satisfy this working dog's energy needs. Routine hip and eye screenings are recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, tapering toward the nose
          Ears: Pendant, triangular, high-set
          Coat: Thick, short, double coat with tricolor pattern
          Tail: Tightly curled over the back
        Measurements:
          Height: 18-23 inches
          Weight: 48-70 lbs

Breed: Aspin
        Size: medium
        Description: The Aspin (Asong Pinoy) is the native mixed-breed dog of the Philippines, known for its resilience, adaptability, and loyal nature.
        Origin: Philippines
        Breed Group: Mixed / Landrace
        Lifespan: 12-16 years
        Temperament: loyal, adaptable, resilient, alert
        Health Considerations: Generally hardy due to natural selection. May still be susceptible to heartworm, tick-borne diseases, and parvovirus common in tropical climates.
        Key Health Tips: Keep up-to-date on core vaccines and anti-parasite treatments. Regular tick and heartworm prevention is essential in tropical environments.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Medium-length, varies widely
          Ears: Semi-erect or dropped, variable
          Coat: Short to medium, dense, various colors
          Tail: Medium-length, curved or straight
        Measurements:
          Height: 16-22 inches
          Weight: 15-40 lbs

Breed: Australian Terrier
        Size: small
        Description: One of the smallest working terriers, the Australian Terrier is spirited and self-confident with a weather-resistant coat suited to tough terrain.
        Origin: Australia
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 11-15 years
        Temperament: spirited, alert, loyal, curious
        Health Considerations: May develop diabetes mellitus, patellar luxation, and Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Thyroid issues have also been noted.
        Key Health Tips: Monitor blood sugar levels if the dog shows unusual thirst or weight changes. Knee check-ups and annual wellness exams are important.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, moderate-length
          Ears: Small, erect, pointed
          Coat: Rough, straight outer coat with soft undercoat
          Tail: Short, docked, carried erect
        Measurements:
          Height: 10-11 inches
          Weight: 14-16 lbs

Breed: Bedlington Terrier
        Size: medium
        Description: A graceful, lamb-like terrier with a distinctive pear-shaped head and crisp curly coat, possessing surprising speed and tenacity beneath its gentle appearance.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 12-16 years
        Temperament: intelligent, good-tempered, loyal, affectionate
        Health Considerations: Prone to Bedlington terrier copper toxicosis, a hereditary liver disease. Also at risk for PRA and renal disease.
        Key Health Tips: DNA test for copper toxicosis before breeding. Annual liver function tests are strongly advised. Monitor diet for copper-rich foods.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Rounded, deep, and well-filled
          Ears: Low-set, pendant, with silky tassel at tip
          Coat: Crisp, curly mix of hard and soft
          Tail: Moderate-length, tapering, low-set
        Measurements:
          Height: 15-17 inches
          Weight: 17-23 lbs

Breed: Bernese Mountain Dog
        Size: large
        Description: A gentle giant from the Swiss Alps, the Bernese Mountain Dog is known for its striking tricolor coat, calm temperament, and deep devotion to family.
        Origin: Switzerland
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 7-10 years
        Temperament: good-natured, calm, strong, affectionate
        Health Considerations: Unfortunately prone to cancer, especially histiocytic sarcoma and mast cell tumors. Also susceptible to hip and elbow dysplasia and bloat.
        Key Health Tips: Early cancer screening is important. Feed multiple small meals to reduce bloat risk. Regular orthopedic evaluations and weight management are essential.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, straight, medium-length
          Ears: Medium-sized, triangular, pendant
          Coat: Thick, moderately long, slightly wavy tricolor
          Tail: Bushy, long, carried low when relaxed
        Measurements:
          Height: 23-27 inches
          Weight: 70-115 lbs

Breed: Blenheim Spaniel
        Size: small
        Description: A variety of the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel with a rich chestnut and white coat, this elegant toy spaniel is affectionate and adaptable.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Toy
        Lifespan: 9-15 years
        Temperament: affectionate, gentle, playful, sociable
        Health Considerations: Prone to mitral valve disease (MVD), syringomyelia, hip dysplasia, and eye conditions. MVD is a leading cause of early death.
        Key Health Tips: Annual cardiac evaluations from age 1. MRI screening for syringomyelia recommended in breeding dogs. Eye exams every year.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Short, tapered
          Ears: Long, silky, pendant
          Coat: Long, silky, chestnut and white
          Tail: Carried level with back, well-feathered
        Measurements:
          Height: 12-13 inches
          Weight: 12-18 lbs

Breed: Border Collie
        Size: medium
        Description: Widely regarded as the world's most intelligent dog breed, the Border Collie is an intense, hardworking herding dog with boundless energy and focus.
        Origin: Scotland / England
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: energetic, alert, intelligent, responsive
        Health Considerations: Prone to Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA), hip dysplasia, epilepsy, and MDR1 gene drug sensitivity. Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL) can also occur.
        Key Health Tips: DNA test for CEA and MDR1 before use in breeding. Provide extensive daily mental and physical stimulation to prevent behavioral issues.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Moderate-length, strong
          Ears: Semi-erect or erect, medium-sized
          Coat: Rough or smooth, double coat
          Tail: Moderately long, low-set, curved at tip
        Measurements:
          Height: 18-22 inches
          Weight: 30-55 lbs

Breed: Border Terrier
        Size: small
        Description: A no-frills working terrier from the Anglo-Scottish border, built for stamina and agility, with a distinctive otter-like head and wiry coat.
        Origin: England / Scotland
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: affectionate, intelligent, obedient, tenacious
        Health Considerations: Generally healthy. May experience hip dysplasia, heart defects, and Canine Epileptoid Cramping Syndrome (CECS or 'Spike's disease').
        Key Health Tips: Monitor for unusual cramping episodes that may indicate CECS. A gluten-free diet may help manage CECS. Regular cardiac checks are advised.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Short, strong
          Ears: Small, V-shaped, folded forward
          Coat: Wiry, dense outer coat with close undercoat
          Tail: Moderately short, thick at base, carried high but not curved
        Measurements:
          Height: 11-16 inches
          Weight: 11-16 lbs

Breed: Boston Bull
        Size: small
        Description: The 'American Gentleman,' the Boston Terrier is a compact, well-mannered companion with a tuxedo-like coat and lively, friendly personality.
        Origin: United States
        Breed Group: Non-Sporting
        Lifespan: 11-13 years
        Temperament: friendly, lively, intelligent, gentle
        Health Considerations: Brachycephalic anatomy leads to respiratory issues. Also prone to cataracts, patellar luxation, deafness, and epilepsy.
        Key Health Tips: Avoid overexertion in heat. Have BAOS evaluated if breathing appears labored. Regular ophthalmology checks due to prominent eyes.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Short, square, brachycephalic
          Ears: Small, erect, fine-textured
          Coat: Short, smooth, tuxedo patterned
          Tail: Short, low-set, either straight or screw
        Measurements:
          Height: 15-17 inches
          Weight: 12-25 lbs

Breed: Bouvier Des Flandres
        Size: large
        Description: A rugged, powerful herding and working dog from Belgium with a thick, rough coat and calm, intelligent disposition ideal for police and military roles.
        Origin: Belgium
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 10-12 years
        Temperament: loyal, intelligent, protective, calm
        Health Considerations: Susceptible to hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, hypothyroidism, and eye conditions including progressive retinal atrophy.
        Key Health Tips: Regular joint screenings and weight management are essential for this large breed. Provide structured exercise and mental challenges daily.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Broad, well-developed, with beard and mustache
          Ears: High-set, triangular, erect when cropped
          Coat: Rough, thick, harsh outer coat with dense undercoat
          Tail: Docked short or naturally short
        Measurements:
          Height: 23-27 inches
          Weight: 70-110 lbs

Breed: Brabancon Griffon
        Size: small
        Description: The smooth-coated variety of the Brussels Griffon, the Brabancon is a charming, monkey-faced companion with a bold personality far exceeding its tiny size.
        Origin: Belgium
        Breed Group: Toy
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: curious, alert, sensitive, loyal
        Health Considerations: Brachycephalic breed prone to breathing difficulties, syringomyelia, eye issues, and patellar luxation.
        Key Health Tips: Avoid excessive heat. Screen for syringomyelia in breeding dogs. Regular eye and respiratory evaluations are recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Very short, pushed-in, brachycephalic
          Ears: Semi-erect or cropped erect, high-set
          Coat: Short, smooth, no beard
          Tail: Short, docked, held high
        Measurements:
          Height: 7-10 inches
          Weight: 8-12 lbs

Breed: Brittany Spaniel
        Size: medium
        Description: An energetic and versatile gun dog from France, the Brittany is known for its hunting prowess, biddable nature, and compact, athletic build.
        Origin: France
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 12-14 years
        Temperament: energetic, bright, fun-loving, adaptable
        Health Considerations: May develop hip dysplasia, epilepsy, and hypothyroidism. Ear infections can occur due to floppy ears.
        Key Health Tips: Clean ears regularly to prevent infections. Provide vigorous daily exercise. Annual thyroid and hip screenings are beneficial.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Medium-length, straight, slightly rounded
          Ears: Short, triangular, slightly rounded, high-set
          Coat: Dense, flat or wavy, orange and white or liver and white
          Tail: Short or absent naturally
        Measurements:
          Height: 17-21 inches
          Weight: 30-40 lbs

Breed: Cardigan
        Size: medium
        Description: The older and larger of the two Corgi breeds, the Cardigan Welsh Corgi is a sturdy, long-bodied herding dog with a full tail and fox-like expression.
        Origin: Wales
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: loyal, affectionate, intelligent, alert
        Health Considerations: Prone to intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) due to long spine, progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), and hip dysplasia.
        Key Health Tips: Minimize jumping on and off furniture to protect the spine. Eye exams annually. Maintain healthy weight to reduce back strain.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Tapering but not pointed, moderate-length
          Ears: Large, prominent, erect with slightly rounded tips
          Coat: Medium-length, dense, hard-textured double coat
          Tail: Long, fox-like, set low
        Measurements:
          Height: 10-13 inches
          Weight: 25-38 lbs

Breed: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
        Size: large
        Description: A powerful, hardworking American retriever bred to hunt waterfowl in the cold, rough waters of the Chesapeake Bay, with a distinctive wavy, oily coat.
        Origin: United States
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 10-13 years
        Temperament: brave, intelligent, affectionate, tenacious
        Health Considerations: Prone to hip and elbow dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, and exercise-induced collapse (EIC).
        Key Health Tips: DNA test for EIC and PRA. Routine joint evaluations due to active lifestyle. Annual eye exams recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Medium-length, tapering muzzle
          Ears: Small to medium, pendant, high-set
          Coat: Short, wavy, oily, water-resistant
          Tail: Medium-length, straight or slightly curved
        Measurements:
          Height: 21-26 inches
          Weight: 55-80 lbs

Breed: Chihuahua
        Size: small
        Description: The world's smallest dog breed, the Chihuahua is a bold and loyal companion with a larger-than-life personality packed into a tiny frame.
        Origin: Mexico
        Breed Group: Toy
        Lifespan: 14-16 years
        Temperament: bold, loyal, sassy, alert
        Health Considerations: Vulnerable to hypoglycemia, patellar luxation, heart disease, and hydrocephalus. Prone to dental overcrowding.
        Key Health Tips: Feed small, frequent meals to prevent hypoglycemia. Regular dental cleanings are critical. Protect from cold due to small body mass.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Short, slightly pointed
          Ears: Large, erect, flaring to sides at a 45-degree angle
          Coat: Smooth or long, soft
          Tail: Medium-length, carried high, sickle-shaped or curled
        Measurements:
          Height: 5-8 inches
          Weight: 2-6 lbs

Breed: Dandie Dinmont
        Size: small
        Description: A distinctive terrier with a long, low body and a large, domed head topped with a silky topknot, originally bred to hunt otters and badgers.
        Origin: Scotland
        Breed Group: Terrier
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: independent, determined, dignified, affectionate
        Health Considerations: Prone to intervertebral disc disease due to elongated spine, glaucoma, and Cushing's disease.
        Key Health Tips: Limit jumping to protect the spinal discs. Routine eye pressure checks due to glaucoma risk. Regular vet checkups for hormonal issues.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, deep, well-developed
          Ears: Pendant, set low, feathered
          Coat: Crisp mixture of hard and soft hair
          Tail: Medium-length, scimitar-shaped
        Measurements:
          Height: 8-11 inches
          Weight: 18-24 lbs

Breed: Doberman
        Size: large
        Description: A sleek, powerful, and highly intelligent breed originally developed as a guard dog in Germany, known for its loyalty and versatility in working roles.
        Origin: Germany
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 10-13 years
        Temperament: loyal, fearless, alert, intelligent
        Health Considerations: Prone to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), von Willebrand's disease, hip dysplasia, and Wobbler syndrome.
        Key Health Tips: Annual cardiac screenings with echocardiogram. DNA test for vWD. Monitor for neck and limb coordination issues indicating Wobbler syndrome.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, strong, parallel to top of skull
          Ears: Erect when cropped, naturally pendant
          Coat: Short, smooth, hard
          Tail: Docked short traditionally, or long and natural
        Measurements:
          Height: 24-28 inches
          Weight: 60-100 lbs

Breed: English Foxhound
        Size: large
        Description: One of the oldest dog breeds, the English Foxhound is a pack hunter bred for stamina and scenting ability, with a harmonious and sociable nature.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Hound
        Lifespan: 10-13 years
        Temperament: sociable, gentle, athletic, stubborn
        Health Considerations: Generally healthy. May develop hip dysplasia and renal disease. Epilepsy has been noted in some bloodlines.
        Key Health Tips: Provide vigorous daily exercise; bored foxhounds can be destructive. Annual hip evaluations and kidney function tests recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, strong, squared off
          Ears: Pendant, rounded at tip, set low
          Coat: Short, dense, glossy
          Tail: Medium-length, carried high, feathered underneath
        Measurements:
          Height: 21-25 inches
          Weight: 60-75 lbs

Breed: English Setter
        Size: large
        Description: A beautiful, elegant gun dog with a silky, speckled coat known as 'belton,' valued for its gentle temperament, grace, and keen bird-hunting ability.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 12-14 years
        Temperament: gentle, friendly, energetic, mischievous
        Health Considerations: Susceptible to hip dysplasia, hypothyroidism, deafness (especially in lightly pigmented dogs), and allergies.
        Key Health Tips: BAER test for deafness in puppies. Annual thyroid and hip evaluations. Regular grooming prevents mat formation in feathered coat.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, sculpted, square-ended
          Ears: Pendant, moderate-length, silky
          Coat: Long, silky, flat, feathered, belton pattern
          Tail: Straight or scimitar-shaped, carried level
        Measurements:
          Height: 24-27 inches
          Weight: 45-80 lbs

Breed: English Springer
        Size: medium
        Description: A cheerful, versatile gun dog known for its enthusiasm and ability to 'spring' game from cover, equally at home in the field and as a devoted companion.
        Origin: England
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 12-14 years
        Temperament: friendly, playful, obedient, energetic
        Health Considerations: Can suffer from hip dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), and Springer rage syndrome (sudden aggression, a temperament disorder).
        Key Health Tips: Seek reputable breeders to avoid rage syndrome lines. Regular eye and hip evaluations. Clean ears weekly to prevent infection.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Medium-length, strong, fairly broad
          Ears: Long, pendant, close to cheeks, feathered
          Coat: Moderately long, dense, flat or wavy
          Tail: Docked or natural, carried horizontally
        Measurements:
          Height: 19-20 inches
          Weight: 40-50 lbs

Breed: Entlebucher
        Size: medium
        Description: The smallest of the four Swiss mountain dogs, the Entlebucher is a compact, agile herder with a tricolor coat and a loyal, energetic personality.
        Origin: Switzerland
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 11-15 years
        Temperament: agile, loyal, independent, energetic
        Health Considerations: May be affected by hip dysplasia and progressive retinal atrophy. Ectopic ureters have also been documented in the breed.
        Key Health Tips: DNA and OFA testing for PRA and hip health before breeding. Provide daily vigorous activity to manage high energy levels.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, not too long
          Ears: Pendant, rounded, medium-sized, set high
          Coat: Short, dense, harsh, tricolor
          Tail: Short, natural bobtail or docked
        Measurements:
          Height: 16-21 inches
          Weight: 40-65 lbs

Breed: Eskimo Dog
        Size: large
        Description: A powerful Nordic sled dog developed by the indigenous peoples of the Arctic, bred for endurance hauling in extreme cold-weather conditions.
        Origin: Arctic regions (Canada / Greenland)
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 12-15 years
        Temperament: alert, loyal, hardy, strong-willed
        Health Considerations: Generally robust. May experience hip dysplasia and inherited eye disorders. Bloat is a concern given their deep chest.
        Key Health Tips: Feed multiple small meals to prevent bloat. Regular exercise is essential. Annual eye and hip evaluations recommended.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Tapering, medium-length, strong
          Ears: Erect, thick, triangular
          Coat: Dense double coat, thick undercoat, weather-resistant
          Tail: Thickly furred, curled over back
        Measurements:
          Height: 20-27 inches
          Weight: 60-105 lbs

Breed: French Bulldog
        Size: small
        Description: A compact, bat-eared charmer with a playful, adaptable nature, the French Bulldog has become one of the most popular breeds worldwide.
        Origin: France
        Breed Group: Non-Sporting
        Lifespan: 10-12 years
        Temperament: adaptable, playful, affectionate, easygoing
        Health Considerations: Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS) is a major concern. Also prone to spinal issues, skin fold dermatitis, and heat sensitivity.
        Key Health Tips: Avoid overexertion and heat. Clean skin folds regularly. BOAS surgical evaluation may be necessary. Avoid air travel in cargo when possible.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Very short, flat, brachycephalic
          Ears: Large, bat-like, erect, rounded at top
          Coat: Short, smooth, fine
          Tail: Short, screw or straight, low-set
        Measurements:
          Height: 11-13 inches
          Weight: 16-28 lbs

Breed: German Shepherd
        Size: large
        Description: One of the world's most versatile and beloved working breeds, known for its intelligence, loyalty, and capability across police, military, and service roles.
        Origin: Germany
        Breed Group: Herding
        Lifespan: 9-13 years
        Temperament: loyal, obedient, alert, courageous
        Health Considerations: Prone to hip and elbow dysplasia, degenerative myelopathy, bloat, and perianal fistulas. Skin and digestive issues also common.
        Key Health Tips: OFA screening for joints before breeding. Degenerative myelopathy DNA testing available. Feed multiple small meals to prevent bloat.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, wedge-shaped, strong
          Ears: Large, erect, pointed
          Coat: Dense, double coat, medium or long
          Tail: Long, bushy, hanging in a slight curve
        Measurements:
          Height: 22-26 inches
          Weight: 50-90 lbs

Breed: German Short-Haired Pointer
        Size: large
        Description: An all-purpose gundog of noble bearing, the GSP is an enthusiastic hunter on land and water with a sleek liver or liver-roan coat and boundless stamina.
        Origin: Germany
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 12-14 years
        Temperament: energetic, intelligent, bold, affectionate
        Health Considerations: Can suffer from hip dysplasia, bloat, heart disease, and cone degeneration (a hereditary eye disorder).
        Key Health Tips: DNA test for cone degeneration. Use slow-feed bowls and structured meals to reduce bloat risk. Provide 2+ hours of exercise daily.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, broad, strong
          Ears: Broad, pendant, close to head
          Coat: Short, thick, water-resistant, liver/liver-roan
          Tail: Docked to 40% in some regions, or natural
        Measurements:
          Height: 21-25 inches
          Weight: 45-70 lbs

Breed: Gordon Setter
        Size: large
        Description: The heaviest of the setter breeds, Scotland's Gordon Setter is a dignified, loyal bird dog with a striking black-and-tan coat and steadfast character.
        Origin: Scotland
        Breed Group: Sporting
        Lifespan: 10-12 years
        Temperament: loyal, confident, alert, intelligent
        Health Considerations: Prone to hip dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, and hypothyroidism. Bloat also possible due to deep chest.
        Key Health Tips: Eye and thyroid exams annually. OFA hip testing recommended. Feed controlled meals with rest after eating to prevent bloat.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, not pointed, slightly broader at top
          Ears: Pendant, close to head, silky
          Coat: Soft, silky, slightly wavy, black with rich tan markings
          Tail: Straight or slightly curved, carried horizontally
        Measurements:
          Height: 23-27 inches
          Weight: 45-80 lbs

Breed: Great Dane
        Size: giant
        Description: Known as the 'Apollo of Dogs,' the Great Dane is a gentle giant with a regal, powerful build and a friendly, patient temperament.
        Origin: Germany
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 7-10 years
        Temperament: friendly, patient, dependable, gentle
        Health Considerations: Highly susceptible to bloat/GDV (life-threatening), dilated cardiomyopathy, hip dysplasia, and wobbler syndrome.
        Key Health Tips: Preventive gastropexy surgery is often recommended. Cardiac evaluations annually. Avoid vigorous exercise immediately before or after meals.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Long, strong, rectangular
          Ears: Medium-sized, pendant, or cropped erect
          Coat: Short, dense, smooth
          Tail: Long, tapering to tip, carried level or slightly curved
        Measurements:
          Height: 28-32 inches
          Weight: 110-175 lbs

Breed: Great Pyrenees
        Size: giant
        Description: A majestic flock guardian from the Pyrenean mountains, the Great Pyrenees is a calm, patient dog with a brilliant white coat built for harsh conditions.
        Origin: France / Spain
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 10-12 years
        Temperament: gentle, confident, patient, independent
        Health Considerations: Prone to hip dysplasia, bloat, osteosarcoma, and patellar luxation. Addison's disease has also been noted.
        Key Health Tips: Regular joint and cardiac screenings. Prevent bloat with meal scheduling. Keep weight in check as extra pounds stress joints significantly.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Broad, medium-length, slightly rounded
          Ears: Medium-sized, triangular, pendant, V-shaped
          Coat: Thick double coat, weather-resistant, white
          Tail: Long, plume-like, curled over back when alert
        Measurements:
          Height: 25-32 inches
          Weight: 85-115 lbs

Breed: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
        Size: large
        Description: The largest of the Swiss mountain dogs, the Greater Swiss is a draft and herding dog with a bold tricolor coat, friendly nature, and impressive strength.
        Origin: Switzerland
        Breed Group: Working
        Lifespan: 8-11 years
        Temperament: bold, faithful, willing, alert
        Health Considerations: Subject to hip and elbow dysplasia, bloat, epilepsy, and urinary incontinence especially in females.
        Key Health Tips: Joint screening before breeding. Manage meal portions and timing to reduce bloat risk. Spay timing can help reduce incontinence in females.
        Physical Traits:
          Snout: Strong, moderate-length
          Ears: Medium-sized, triangular, pendant
          Coat: Dense, medium-length, tricolor

# DogScan AI System Guide

DogScan AI helps users scan dog photos for breed and skin disease insights, save scan history, and optionally contribute approved scan snapshots to improve the system.

## Main Navigation

- Dashboard: `/dashboard`
  - See profile summary, quick actions, and recent scans.
  - Open scan workspace from "Scan New Dog".
- Assistant: `/assistant`
  - General AI assistant chat for dog care, breed info, disease education, and app tutorials.
- Library: `/doglibrary`
  - Explore dog breeds and detailed breed information.
- History: `/history`
  - Review saved scans, confidence, and contribution review status.
- Profile: `/profile`
  - Update username, email, password, and account details.
- Contributors Leaderboard: `/contributors`
  - Public leaderboard of users with approved contribution counts.

## Scan Workflow

1. Open scan workspace from Dashboard or public demo section.
2. Choose scan mode:
   - Breed Scan: predicts likely breed mix, plus emotion and age.
   - Disease Scan: predicts possible skin condition matches.
3. Upload a clear dog image and run scan.
4. Review top results and confidence values.
5. Save result to history if logged in.
6. Optionally toggle contribution before saving a breed scan.

## Contribution Workflow (Snapshot-Based)

- A user can share a saved breed scan for review.
- Admin reviews pending contributions in the admin panel.
- Admin can approve (with final breed) or reject (with reason).
- Approved contributions are counted in the contributors leaderboard.

## Public Demo Rules

- Public demo supports limited scans per device.
- Public disease scan requires login.
- Public users should sign up to unlock full history and contribution features.

## Assistant Scope

- The assistant can explain:
  - Scan results and what confidence means.
  - Breed traits, temperament, and care basics.
  - Disease-result education and general next steps.
  - DogScan AI app tutorials and route navigation.
- The assistant should not provide veterinary diagnosis.
- For health concerns, it should advise consulting a licensed veterinarian.
